z: Charge number of the particle (its charge is ze)
Charge number of the particle (1 for a proton)

A: Atomic mass (in Z/A, per gram per mole)
E': Kinetic energy, the variable of integration
I: Mean excitation energy of the material
R: CSDA range, the path a particle travels while slowing to rest at the mean rate
divide by the density for cm
R_20: Depth beyond the peak where the dose has fallen to 20 % of the peak
R_80: Depth beyond the peak where the dose has fallen to 80 % of the peak
R_90: Depth beyond the peak where the dose has fallen to 90 % of the peak
S: Stopping power, the mean energy a particle loses per unit path, −dE/dx
divided by ρ it is the mass stopping power, MeV cm²/g
W_max: Largest energy one collision can give an electron
Z: Atomic number (in Z/A, electrons per atom)
bar z: Mean depth where the simulated protons stopped
beta: Speed of the particle as a fraction of the speed of light, v/c
gamma: Lorentz factor of the particle, 1/√(1 − β²)
r: Residual range, the range a proton still has left
sigma: Spread (standard deviation) of the depths where the protons stopped
t_w: Water equivalent thickness of a slab, the depth of water that takes away the same energy
x: Path length traveled in the material
